REGULATION (most material this week): US — a new White House executive order, 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security' (signed June 2026), extends the federal push begun by the 11 Dec 2025 EO that seeks to preempt state AI laws via a DOJ litigation task force. State laws stand in the short term: Colorado's AI Act takes effect 30 June 2026 (delayed; disclosure obligations) — relevant only if a future SageReasoning offering reaches US users, but it signals the federal-vs-state friction to watch. AUSTRALIA: the first mandatory requirement under the 'Policy for the responsible use of AI in government' begins 15 June 2026 — now ~1 week out. It binds Australian Public Service agencies (mandatory foundational AI training for all staff, an AI-incident process, a public/staff reporting pathway), NOT private companies — so SageReasoning is not bound, but it marks the AU direction. EU: the Digital Omnibus Parliament vote is expected ~7 July 2026, with formal adoption before the 2 Aug trigger; new Article 5 prohibitions on NCII/CSAM (adjacent to R17), high-risk Annex III deferred to 2 Dec 2027, Annex I to 2 Aug 2028. SOLO-FOUNDER ECONOMICS (refined): a full agentic stack is now cited at ~$75–150/month (replacing ~$600–1,000/month of part-time VA work); commentary stresses GOVERNED systems with audit trails and human checkpoints over tool-stacking — congruent with Sage Ops + R5/R16. FUNDING: Carta Q1 2026 unchanged (AI ~50% of pre-seed dollars, ~33% of total VC, ~42% seed premium, median pre-money ~$17.9M; $1M–$2.5M band down to 18%). RISKS — FOUNDER ATTENTION: AU 15 June (signal, not obligation); EU Omnibus 7 July vote; Colorado 30 June. OPPORTUNITY: the cheap, governed agent stack is a near-zero-marginal-cost lift for the founder's own Sage Ops tooling.

support.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. FRESH DATA (most material this week): a RAND study (released early June 2026) finds ~19.2% of US 12–21-year-olds (~8.2M) used AI chatbots for mental-health advice in 2025, up from ~13% a year earlier; 63% kept that use secret; and 91.7% rated the advice 'helpful' — which researchers attribute partly to sycophancy rather than quality. This directly reinforces R20 (vulnerable-user detection — note the secrecy signal as a design challenge) and R19 (mirror principle / anti-sycophancy). REGULATION tightening further: Tennessee SB 1580 (AI may not present as a licensed mental-health professional) takes effect 1 July 2026; Oregon SB 1546 (Mar 2026) adds disclosure + suicide-ideation detection + crisis referral; Colorado's AI Act disclosure obligations begin 30 June 2026. New York (Nov 2025) and California SB 243 (Jan 2026) remain the live de-facto R20a templates. Bill counts vary by source (Orrick/MultiState cite ~34 states / 98 bills; other tallies ~43 states / 240+) — the direction is unambiguous: a rising disclosure + crisis-referral floor for human-facing tools. INCIDENTS: the International AI Safety Report 2026 (Bengio-led, 3 Feb) flags companion-app psychological dependence (evidence early/mixed); Google/Character.AI settled the Florida-teen lawsuit (a first major US psychological-harm challenge); Stanford documents AI-relationship 'delusional spirals' — all adjacent to R19/R20 and the synchronous distress-classifier discipline (PR3). ACCESSIBILITY: WCAG 3.0's March-2026 Working Draft (174 requirements; graded scores replacing pass/fail) advances, but Candidate Recommendation is ~Q4 2027 and W3C Recommendation not before 2028 — so WCAG 2.1 / 2.2 AA remains the live legal standard and SageReasoning's target; no change. RISK — FOUNDER ATTENTION: the disclosure + crisis-referral + 'not a licensed professional' compliance floor for human-facing tools is rising (TN 1 July, CO 30 June). OPPORTUNITY: the honest-positioning posture (R18a/R19) plus synchronous safety-by-design align with both the new data (secrecy/sycophancy) and the regulatory templates.
